purpose: A one-way valve for electricity. Current flows easily from Anode to Cathode, but is blocked from flowing backwards. It protects microcontrollers from inductive voltage spikes, prevents damage from backwards batteries, and directs power flow.

whenToUse.scenario: Motors, Solenoids, or Relays (Flyback / Snubber Protection)
whenToUse.why: Inductive coils store energy in a magnetic field. When power is cut, this field collapses, generating reverse voltage spikes of 50V to 400V. A diode across the coil harmlessly recirculates this spike, preventing burned Arduino pins or blown transistors.
whenToUse.recommended: 1N4007 (for slow coils) or 1N5819 Schottky (for fast PWM)

whenToUse.why: Plugging in a 9V battery or 12V adapter backwards instantly fries microcontrollers. Placing a diode in series on the positive power line completely blocks reverse current.
whenToUse.recommended: 1N5817 or SS34 Schottky diode (low ~0.2V to 0.3V drop so you waste minimal battery power)

whenToUse.scenario: Dual Power Supply OR-ing (USB vs Battery)
whenToUse.why: When you want a device to seamlessly switch between USB 5V and a backup battery without one power source back-feeding into the other.
whenToUse.recommended: Schottky diodes on each power rail (e.g. 1N5819)

whenToUse.why: When you need to cap a fluctuating sensor voltage at a safe 3.3V or 5.1V ceiling so it cannot exceed the Arduino pin's absolute maximum rating.
whenToUse.recommended: 3.3V or 5.1V Zener Diode (with series current-limiting resistor)

whenToUse.why: Protecting external sensors and exposed data lines (like USB or RS485) from human static shocks (ESD) or lightning surges.

basics.title: Anode (+) vs Cathode (-)
basics.text: Current flows from the Anode to the Cathode. On physical cylindrical diodes, a printed silver or white stripe marks the CATHODE end. Remember: Stripe = Negative / Exit.

basics.title: Forward Voltage Drop (Vf)
basics.text: Every diode takes a small voltage toll to open the gate: ~0.7V for standard silicon (1N4007), ~0.2V–0.3V for Schottky (1N5819), and 1.8V–3.2V for LEDs. Choose Schottky when every tenth of a volt matters on battery projects.

basics.title: Reverse Breakdown & Leakage
basics.text: If reverse voltage exceeds the diode's rating (Peak Inverse Voltage / PIV), it breaks down. 1N4007 handles up to 1000V in reverse, while low-voltage Schottky diodes handle 20V to 40V.

basics.title: Zener Diodes Break Down on Purpose
basics.text: Unlike standard diodes, Zener diodes are intentionally operated in REVERSE bias. When reverse voltage reaches the rated Zener voltage (e.g. 5.1V), it conducts steadily, clamping the voltage.

types.name: Standard Rectifier (1N4001–1N4007)
types.looks: Black plastic cylinder (DO-41 package) with a silver band marking the cathode.
pros: Handles huge reverse voltages (up to 1000V for 1N4007)
cons: Too slow for high-frequency PWM switching
uses: Flyback snubber for DC relays and solenoids

types.name: Schottky Diode (1N5817 / 1N5819 / SS34)
types.looks: Black DO-41 or surface-mount SMA/SMB package with silver/white band.
pros: Low voltage loss saves battery run-time
Fast switching handles high-frequency PWM and DC-DC converters
cons: Slightly higher reverse leakage current at hot temperatures
uses: Output rectifiers in DC-DC buck/boost converters

types.name: Zener Diode (e.g. 3.3V / 5.1V BZX55)
types.voltageDrop: Forward: 0.7V | Reverse breakdown: Rated Zener voltage
types.looks: Small red or orange clear glass cylinder with a black band marking the cathode.
pros: Provides reliable voltage clamping and references
cons: Cannot supply high currents directly (requires series resistor)
Wastes current as heat when clamping
uses: Over-voltage input clamp on analog pins

types.name: Fast Small-Signal Diode (1N4148)
types.looks: Tiny clear orange/red glass bead with a black stripe.
pros: Perfect for signal lines and logic matrixes
cons: Cannot handle heavy power loads (max 200–300 mA)

types.name: TVS Diode (Transient Voltage Suppressor)
types.maxCurrent: Up to hundreds of Amperes for nanoseconds
types.looks: Black rectangular diode package or bidirectional dual-lead package.
pros: Clamps lethal electrostatic discharge (ESD) in picoseconds
Protects exposed connectors from lightning and static
cons: Only for brief surges, will burn out under continuous over-voltage
uses: Outdoor sensor wires and RS485 communication lines

examples.title: Flyback Snubber on Relay / Motor Coil
examples.description: How to wire a 1N4007 or 1N5819 flyback diode in reverse-parallel across a DC inductive load (motor, relay, solenoid) so inductive back-EMF spikes are safely extinguished.
code: // Flyback Diode Demo: Safe Inductive Load Switching
// The diode is connected in REVERSE across the coil (+ to stripe, - to anode).
// During normal operation, no current passes through the diode.
// When the pin turns OFF, the coil's collapsing magnetic field creates a reverse
// spike that circulates safely through the diode instead of killing the transistor.
Serial.println(F("Inductive load driver with flyback protection active."));
Serial.println(F("Load de-energized (Flyback spike clamped by diode)..."));
